scope: Durable domain events, revoked-review claim recovery, task-type context recipes and saved checkpoints. Existing work and concurrent browser implementation were preserved.
claimContract: review.start returns claimId; review.submit, review context and review checkpoints require the current claimId.
verifiedBehaviors: Handler effects and cursor roll back together; retry commits once.
A failed consumer does not block independent consumers.
Unloaded consumers resume durable progress after reload/restart.
Revocation remains effective while Domain Events and Reviews are unloaded.
Revoked initiators do not prevent trusted review cleanup.
Review recovery preserves evidence and task revision; stale claims fail.
Existing review databases migrate open claims without rewriting verdicts.
Required context, budgets, scope, source hashes, recipe versions and immutable packages are enforced.
Custom task types register recipes without adapter plugins.
Replacement context includes recovery cause, saved checkpoints, pinned background and evidence.
Context/checkpoint tools work through real local HTTP/MCP and context packages survive two restarts.
limits: Single application runtime per database; synchronous local event handlers.
Event history retained in full; no pruning or automatic failed-event skipping.
UTF-8 context inputs and explicit character budgets.
No automatic agent launcher, work leases, remote cancellation or production Nisa rollout.
